label: Compatible cover and space
native_anchor:
We also
ensured that scenarios were feasible at the RHHU level,
meaning that there was enough available and compatible
surface area to support the increased wetland cover and
contributing area. The increase in wetland cover was thus
limited to replacing forest, agriculture, open lands and bare
review_note: Source-specific compatible land-cover availability within RHHU; constrained scenario, not universal conversion permission.

label: Impervious-surface exclusion
native_anchor:
soil. We acknowledge that replacing impervious surfaces
with wetlands could have led to greater impacts (and the
identiﬁcation of lower restoration targets), but we decided to
test scenarios that would be easier for decision-makers to
envision (due to the high socio-economic cost of imper-
vious surface removal).

label: Existingwetland location/type allocation
native_anchor:
We generated a range of wetland-based exploratory
scenarios to investigate how much restoration would be
needed to maintain current hydrological regimes under
future climate conditions. Wetland restoration was simu-
lated by increasing wetland areas, and their respective
contributing areas, by 20, 50, 100, and 150% in each sub-
watershed. We distributed these increases across isolated
and riparian wetlands according to their current relative
abundance (in the reference period) and location.
review_note: Scenario allocation by existing location/type; not existing-footprint hardmask.

rather than downstream, and a greater contribution of

2016).
